fact: Digital Policy Alert records that Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024, adopted by Parliament on 4 April 2024, entered into force on 24 July 2024 and requires data controllers and processors to store locally collected personal data on servers in Ethiopia.

Digital Policy Alert states that the Personal Data Protection Proclamation, implemented in July 2024, requires controllers and processors to store personal data collected locally on a server or data centre within Ethiopia.

Digital Policy Alert states that in August 2021 the Ethiopian Communications Authority adopted a consumer rights directive requiring telecom providers to process consumer personal data only on servers or data centres in Ethiopia.

Digital Policy Alert states that the Ethiopian Communications Authority, which issued the telecom localisation directive, oversees compliance with data protection rules; it adds that no official enforcement sources are published.

Birr Metrics reports that Ethiopia's Personal Data Protection Proclamation of 2024 mandates that data collected domestically be stored within the country, with cross-border transfers permitted only under strict conditions.
Xalam Analytics says the Personal Data Protection Proclamation of 2024 requires companies to host Ethiopian citizen data within the country.

The law firm Haymanot & Advocates says National Bank of Ethiopia Directive No. SBB/94/2025 requires all banks, foreign subsidiaries and branches included, to store and process customer and core banking data, primary and backup, within Ethiopia.
The same source says the National Bank of Ethiopia issued the Directive for the banks it licenses and that transfers of core banking data abroad need its prior written approval.
